method.method_draft: First describe the visual trend: as light intensity increases, the rate of photosynthesis increases, but after a certain point the graph levels off. Interpret the initial slope as light being the limiting factor. Interpret the plateau as saturation of the light-harvesting apparatus in the thylakoid membranes, meaning the photosynthetic machinery cannot make use of extra light, so the rate stops increasing.

planner_metadata.image_role: Read the graph axes: the y-axis is rate of photosynthesis and the x-axis is light intensity. Observe that the curve rises steeply at low light intensity and then becomes a horizontal plateau at higher light intensity.
planner_metadata.text_role: Use the question wording to focus on explaining the shape of the graph—why the rate increases at first and then stops increasing—rather than calculating a numerical value.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Use the biological rule that increasing light raises photosynthesis only while the light-harvesting/light-reaction machinery can absorb and use more photons; once the thylakoid membrane photosystems/electron transport components are saturated, additional light cannot further increase the rate.
